articles.title: Homes evacuated in Rochdale after car crashes into house and causes gas leak
articles.excerpt: Emergency services evacuated around 55 residents after a car collided with a property on Halifax Road, leading to a gas leak.
articles.content_html:
Emergency services evacuated approximately 55 residents in Rochdale after a car crashed into a house on Halifax Road early on Saturday morning, October 31. The incident, which occurred around 2:25am, resulted in a confirmed gas leak, prompting a swift response from local authorities.

Greater Manchester Police reported that they were called to the scene following the collision. A 50-metre cordon was established around the area while emergency services worked to secure the site.

Two individuals were taken to hospital as a precautionary measure, although their conditions have not been disclosed.

Fire crews from Rochdale and Littleborough fire stations attended the scene with three fire engines. They used specialist equipment to ensure the area was safe and assisted in the evacuation of nearby properties due to the gas leak caused by the crash.

Firefighters remained on site for approximately four-and-a-half hours to manage the situation.

The road has since reopened, and residents have been allowed to return to their homes. This incident underscores the critical role of emergency services in responding to unexpected hazards and ensuring community safety.
articles.social_headline: Residents evacuated after car crashes into house in Rochdale, causing gas leak.

articles.title: Birthday cards for Wendy: family’s heartfelt appeal ahead of her 79th birthday
articles.excerpt: Wendy Bamford turns 79 on Wednesday 4 November, and her birthday wish is simple: cards filled with kind words.
articles.content_html:
A family is inviting the community to help make Wendy Bamford’s 79th birthday special by sending her a card filled with a few kind words.

Wendy turns 79 on Wednesday 4 November. Her son Stephen Bamford shared the appeal after she moved to Springhill Hospice in Rochdale.

When he asked his mum what she wanted for her birthday, or whether there was anything she would like to do, her answer was simple: lots of birthday cards, so she could sit and read the lovely messages inside. It is the only thing she has asked for, Stephen said.

A little kindness could mean so much

Stephen is welcoming cards from people who know Wendy and those who have never met her but would like to brighten her day.

“A few kind words might seem like a small thing, but they would mean the world to her right now,” he wrote.

In an update, Stephen thanked everyone for their comments and messages, explaining that the response had become too large for him to answer individually. He shared two addresses where cards can be sent.

Where to send a birthday card

Cards can be addressed directly to Wendy at:

Wendy Bamford, Room 10, Springhill Hospice, Broad Lane, Rochdale

Alternatively, cards can be sent to Stephen through the Littleborough collection address:

For Wendy Bamford, care of Stephen Bamford, Cryers Butchers, 39 Victoria Street, Littleborough, OL15 8BA

Stephen has promised to make sure his mum receives them, ready to open and enjoy on her birthday. Anyone wishing to take part is encouraged to allow time for delivery.

Source: Stephen Bamford’s public birthday appeal and follow-up, supplied to Rochdale Daily. Photograph supplied with the appeal.

articles.title: St Luke’s Church in Deeplish announces upcoming services and community events
articles.excerpt: St Luke’s Church in Deeplish will hold a Morning Praise service on November 1, followed by a series of community activities throughout the month.
articles.content_html:
St Luke’s Church in Deeplish is set to hold a service of Morning Praise on November 1 at 10am, officiated by Reader Sue Horobin. This service will be followed by tea and coffee, providing an opportunity for attendees to socialise and connect with one another.

On November 4, the church will host a Bible Study at 10am, followed by another Morning Praise service at 11am, officiated by Revd Natty Gray. The church welcomes both regular members and newcomers to join their friendly congregation.

Last Sunday, the church celebrated Holy Communion, officiated by Revd Ian Butterworth, and will continue with communion next week, led by Kirsten Rutherford. After each service, refreshments will be available, allowing for fellowship among attendees.

In addition to the services, the church is selling some of its youth group costumes, which have attracted interest from societies worldwide, including buyers from Germany, Italy, Norway, and America. This initiative not only helps clear space in the church but also supports community engagement.

articles.title: Charlie Tasker thriving during loan spell at Rochdale from Brighton
articles.excerpt: Charlie Tasker, on loan from Brighton, is making a strong impact at Rochdale, adapting well to a new position and earning the fans' support.
articles.content_html:
Charlie Tasker, a 20-year-old defender on loan from Brighton & Hove Albion, is quickly making his mark at Rochdale.

Since joining the League Two club, he has become a regular starter and has taken on a new role on the left side of defence, showcasing his adaptability and skill.

Tasker has expressed his excitement about his first loan experience, stating that he wanted to join a club where he would have a good chance of playing.

He noted that Rochdale's style of play is attractive and reminiscent of Brighton's, which has helped him settle in more easily.

The young defender has already garnered support from Rochdale fans, who appreciate his performances despite the team's recent 5-0 defeat at home.

Tasker has yet to return to his previous club in Mile Oak, indicating his commitment to making the most of his time in Rochdale.

As he continues to adapt to his new environment, Tasker is focused on contributing to Rochdale's success this season. His positive attitude and willingness to embrace the challenge of EFL football could prove beneficial for both him and the club moving forward.

articles.title: Heywood’s Little Play Town put up for sale as owner reassures families it will stay open
articles.excerpt: Owner Jackie is seeking a buyer after four years, with Little Play Town remaining open and existing party bookings going ahead as planned.
articles.content_html:
Little Play Town in Heywood has been put up for sale, with owner Jackie reassuring families that the children’s role play business will remain open and existing party bookings will go ahead as planned.

Announcing the decision, Jackie said she was selling for personal reasons after four years of building the business alongside her team.

“This is something I never thought I’d be writing, and it’s been an incredibly difficult decision to make,” she said.

Jackie described Little Play Town as her “pride and joy” and thanked the staff, customers and families who have supported it.

She stressed that the sale announcement does not mean the venue is closing. Sessions will continue as normal, and families with parties booked do not need to change their plans.

The search is now on for a new owner to take over the established leasehold business. Jackie said a support package lasting up to three months would be available to help the buyer settle in.

The announcement highlights the existing staff team, supportive customer base and opportunities to introduce additional themed events, sessions and experiences. Jackie also described the landlord as proactive and supportive.

She hopes to find someone who will build on the business’s first four years and continue providing a place for children to play and make memories.

Anyone interested in buying Little Play Town can register their interest by emailing info@littleplaytownheywood.co.uk.

For local families, the immediate message is that the venue remains open and booked celebrations will continue as planned. What have your children enjoyed most about visiting Little Play Town? Share your memories in the comments.

articles.title: Plans approved for 27 affordable homes in Rochdale town centre
articles.excerpt: Great Places Housing Group's proposal for 27 affordable homes on Drake Street has received approval from Rochdale Council, aiming to address local housing needs.
articles.content_html:
Plans for 27 new affordable homes in Rochdale town centre have been approved by Rochdale Council.

The development, proposed by Great Places Housing Group, will be located on vacant land at 206-208 Drake Street, which has been unused for several years after the demolition of a former DVLA test centre.

The approved scheme includes a three-storey apartment building with 23 apartments and a 2.5-storey terrace of four family homes.

The site, situated at the corner of Drake Street and Broadfield Stile, is adjacent to the Grade II-registered Broadfield Park, providing good access to local services and public transport.

Supporting documents from Paddock Johnson architects highlight that the project will provide 100% affordable housing for social rent, exceeding local policy requirements and responding to an identified housing need within Rochdale.

The redevelopment aims to make effective use of an underused urban site, contributing to the local community's housing stock.

The council previously granted planning permission on appeal for a different scheme of 17 homes, which did not proceed. The new development is expected to enhance the area and provide substantial public benefit, with construction timelines yet to be confirmed.

articles.title: Steven's 15-stone weight loss transformation at Heywood Sports Village
articles.excerpt: Steven's remarkable journey to lose 15 stone has transformed his health and confidence, allowing him to enjoy life with his family.
articles.content_html:
Steven, a member of Heywood Sports Village, has achieved a remarkable transformation by losing 15 stone, significantly improving his health and quality of life. His journey began when he realised that everyday activities had become increasingly difficult, impacting his ability to enjoy family life.

At his heaviest, Steven struggled with simple tasks such as walking upstairs and playing with his children. The turning point came after witnessing his wife's successful health transformation, which inspired him to take control of his own wellbeing.

He sought guidance from Personal Trainer Alex at Heywood Sports Village, where he received structured training and nutritional support.

Throughout his journey, Steven faced challenges, including moments when motivation dipped. However, the support from his family and the gym community helped him stay focused on his long-term goals.

Today, he feels fitter, stronger, and more confident, enjoying activities that were once daunting. He can now buy clothes from regular high street shops and participate in family holidays without feeling self-conscious.

Steven advises others looking to start their fitness journey to make small changes and set clear personal goals. He emphasises the importance of seeking support and working with a coach to achieve lasting results.

His story serves as an inspiration for those in the community looking to improve their health.

articles.title: Middleton designated as mayoral development area to boost regeneration
articles.excerpt: Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig has designated Middleton as a mayoral development area, aiming to enhance economic development and housing in the town.
articles.content_html:
Middleton has been officially designated as a mayoral development area by Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig, marking a significant step forward in the town's regeneration efforts.

This decision follows a six-week public consultation and was approved by the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) last month, with Rochdale Council also endorsing the proposal.

The establishment of the Middleton Co-operative Mayoral Development Corporation is expected to accelerate economic development and regeneration in the area. The GMCA highlighted that this designation presents a substantial opportunity to improve Middleton town centre and its surrounding communities.

The new development corporation aims to attract both public and private investment, facilitating the construction of approximately 1,500 new homes, including affordable housing. This initiative is part of a broader strategy to enhance the living conditions and economic prospects for local residents.

The Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government has been notified of this designation, which will be formalised by an official order.

This development is crucial for Middleton, as it seeks to revitalise the town and provide much-needed housing and services for its community.

evidence_sources.captured_text: Town’s regeneration journey takes another step forward - Rochdale Times Skip to content LATEST NEWS Town’s regeneration journey takes another step forward Regeneration of Middleton has moved a step closer after the town was identified as a mayoral development area by Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig. Following a six-week public consultation, a report was submitted to a meeting of the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) last month when the proposed designation was approved and subsequently endorsed by Rochdale Council. The Mayor notified the Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government of the designation. The Secretary of State will, by Order, establish a Mayoral development corporation for the Area. The name to be given to the Mayoral development corporation is the Middleton Co-operative Mayoral Development Corporation. Designating the town as a mayoral development corporation is expected to help speed up furthering economic development and regeneration in Middleton. The GMCA said: “The area presents a significant opportunity to improve Middleton town centre and its surrounding communities. “Establishing the Middleton Co-operative Mayoral Development Corporation will help attract public and private investment, bring forward new development and support the delivery of around 1,500 new homes, including affordable homes. READ MORE: New trial gives children better mental health and social care support Middleton has been identified as a mayoral development area. Image: GMCA “It will also strengthen the town’s commercial and leisure offer, improve public spaces and infrastructure, create jobs and support better services for local people. “Without a dedicated delivery vehicle, Middleton would risk missing the opportunity to coordinate investment, accelerate regeneration and overcome barriers relating to land, infrastructure, viability, funding and delivery.” The corporation will be underpinned by co-operative principles, giving residents, businesses and community organisations a meaningful voice in shaping the regeneration programme. This approach will help ensure that investment delivers inclusive growth, social wellbeing, community pride and benefits that extend across Middleton and the wider borough. The corporation is expected to be established in early 2027. It will provide a single, focused body for local decision-making and engagement with residents, communities, government departments, public agencies, landowners, developers and investors. Working alongside Rochdale Council, Rochdale Development Agency and GMCA, it will coordinate delivery and help secure public and private investment to realise the shared vision for regeneration across the Area.
